'''Jennifer Wilcox''' is an American [[chemical engineer]] and an expert in  [[carbon capture and storage]] and the [[Carbon dioxide removal|removal]] of CO<sub>2</sub> from the atmosphere.<ref>{{cite news|accessdate=2020-01-20|title=Greenhouse gases must be scrubbed from the air, Greenhouse gases must be scrubbed from the air|url=https://www.economist.com/briefing/2017/11/16/greenhouse-gases-must-be-scrubbed-from-the-air|newspaper=The Economist|issn=0013-0613}}</ref> She is the Presidential Distinguished Professor of Chemical Engineering and Energy Policy at [[University of Pennsylvania]] and a former James H. Manning Chaired Professor of Chemical Engineering at [[Worcester Polytechnic Institute]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.wpi.edu/people/faculty/jlwilcox|title=jlwilcox|website=WPI|language=en|access-date=2020-01-20}}</ref> Wilcox conducts research focused on minimizing the environmental and climate impacts of our dependence on fossil fuels.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Internationally Renowned Expert on Capturing and Storing Carbon Dioxide and Other Fossil Fuel Pollutants Is Named WPI's New Manning Professor|url=https://www.wpi.edu/news/internationally-renowned-expert-capturing-and-storing-carbon-dioxide-and-other-fossil-fuel|access-date=2021-05-10|website=WPI|date=August 2018 |language=en}}</ref> In January 2021, she became acting [[Assistant Secretary for Fossil Energy|Assistant Secretary for Fossil Energy and Carbon Management]]<ref>{{Cite web|title=Assistant Secretaries for Fossil Energy|url=https://www.energy.gov/fe/assistant-secretaries-fossil-energy|access-date=2021-03-06|website=Energy.gov|language=en}}</ref> and Principal Deputy Assistant Secretary (PDAS) for Fossil Energy and Carbon Management.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Dr. Jennifer Wilcox|url=https://www.energy.gov/fe/contributors/dr-jennifer-wilcox|access-date=2021-03-06|website=Energy.gov|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|date=2021-01-27|title=RELEASE: WRI Experts Join Biden-Harris Administration at U.S. Department of Energy|url=https://www.wri.org/news/2021/01/release-wri-experts-join-biden-harris-administration-us-department-energy|access-date=2021-03-06|website=World Resources Institute|language=en}}</ref>

== Early life and education ==
Wilcox was born on July 5, 1976, and grew up in a rural part of central Maine in a house that was on 22 acres of land with a stream.<ref name=":0">{{cite web|url=https://tanyaprive.com/jennifer-wilcox/|title=Synthetic Forests: A Possible Way To Remove CO2 From The Air|website=TanyaPrive|date=10 October 2019 }}</ref> Her parents grew their own food in the summer and maintained a well on the property, exposing Wilcox to an independent living that shaped her appreciation for nature and to not take the Earth's resources for granted.<ref name=":0" />

When Wilcox found out her rural high school, [[Oak Hill High School (Maine)|Oak Hill High School]] in [[Wales, Maine]], didn't offer AP [[calculus]] classes that she would need to get into a selective college, she bought a calculus book and with three other students successfully convinced their principal to let them teach themselves calculus so they could take the [[AP exam]]. Wilcox also asked her high school Latin teacher to continue teaching her Latin during her junior and senior years as an independent study, which the teacher happily assisted. Wilcox was so proficient in Latin she taught younger students when the teacher was on leave. The extra efforts paid off as Wilcox was accepted into the women's [[liberal arts]] college of [[Wellesley College]] in Wellesley, Massachusetts.<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":3">{{Cite web |date=2023-06-01 |title=Teaching to Understand: Professor and Climate Scientist Jennifer… |url=https://www.wellesley.edu/news/teaching-to-understand-professor-and-climate-scientist-jennifer-wilcox-98 |access-date=2025-11-21 |website=Wellesley |language=en-US}}</ref> She graduated from Wellesley in 1998.<ref name=":3" />

She enrolled in the [[Ph.D.]] program in chemical engineering at the University of Arizona and received both her [[Master's degree|master's]] and Ph.D. in four years while continuing to wait tables and teach at a community college.<ref name=":0" />

== Career ==
After receiving her Ph.D. in 2004, Wilcox worked as an Assistant Professor of Chemical Engineering at [[Worcester Polytechnic]] from 2004 to 2008.<ref name=":2" /> She then took on the position of Assistant Professor of Energy Resources Engineering at [[Stanford University]] from 2008 to 2016.<ref name=":2" /> In 2016, Wilcox became an Associate Professor of Chemical and Biological Engineering at [[Colorado School of Mines]], assuming the position of the Interim Department Head in 2017.<ref name=":2" /> In 2018, she left Mines to assume the James H. Manning Chaired Professorship of Chemical Engineering at Worcester Polytechnic Institute.<ref name=":2">[https://chemeng.mines.edu/wp-content/uploads/sites/25/2019/11/CBEN-History-Appendix-II.pdf Appendix II, Faculty Curriculum Vitae.] Colorado School of Mines, Retrieved April 24, 2022.</ref> In 2020, she left Worcester Polytechnic Institute to join the Chemical and Biomolecular Engineering Department and Kleinman Center for Energy Policy at the University of Pennsylvania.

Wilcox served on a number of committees including the [[National Academy of Sciences]] and the [[American Physical Society]]. She receives funding for her research through the [[National Science Foundation]], [[United States Department of Energy|Department of Energy]] and the private sector.

She spoke at the April 2018 [[TED (conference)|TED]] talk<ref>{{citation|first1=Jennifer|last1=Wilcox|title=A new way to remove CO2 from the atmosphere|date=5 July 2018 |url=https://www.ted.com/talks/jennifer_wilcox_a_new_way_to_remove_co2_from_the_atmosphere|via=www.ted.com}}</ref> about her research on [[Direct air capture|Direct Air Capture]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Internationally Renowned Expert on Capturing and Storing Carbon Dioxide and Other Fossil Fuel Pollutants Is Named WPI's New Manning Professor|url=https://www.wpi.edu/news/internationally-renowned-expert-capturing-and-storing-carbon-dioxide-and-other-fossil-fuel|access-date=2021-03-31|website=WPI|date=August 2018 |language=en}}</ref>

In 2024, Wilcox took on the position of Chief Scientist at Isometric, a carbon registry.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Pontecorvo |first=Emily |title=Jennifer Wilcox on Building the First U.S. Carbon Removal Office |work=Heatmap |url=https://heatmap.news/climate/jennifer-wilcox-carbon-removal |access-date=11 June 2024}}</ref>

== Awards and honors ==
Wilcox represented the National Science Foundation as a "New Face of Engineering for 2006", where she was featured in [[USA Today]].<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|title=Internationally Renowned Expert on Capturing and Storing Carbon Dioxide and Other Fossil Fuel Pollutants Is Named WPI's New Manning Professor|url=https://www.wpi.edu/news/internationally-renowned-expert-capturing-and-storing-carbon-dioxide-and-other-fossil-fuel|access-date=2020-01-13|website=WPI|date=August 2018 |language=en}}</ref> She also won the American Chemical Society Petroleum Research Fund Young Investigator Award,<ref name=":1" /> the [[United States Army Research Laboratory|Army Research Office]] Young Investigator Award,<ref name=":1" /> and the Air & Waste Management Association<ref>{{Cite web|title=Air & Waste Management Association|url=https://www.awma.org/|access-date=2021-09-22|website=www.awma.org}}</ref> Stern Award.<ref name=":1" /><ref>{{Cite web|title=A&WMA - Arthur C. Stern Award for Distinguished Paper|url=https://www.awma.org/content.asp?contentid=202|access-date=2021-09-22|website=www.awma.org|language=en}}</ref> In 2023, she was named one of the [[Time (magazine)|Time]] 100 Climate leaders.<ref>{{cite web | title=TIME100 Climate 2023: Jennifer Wilcox | date=16 November 2023 | url=https://time.com/collection/time100-climate/6333059/jennifer-wilcox/ }}</ref> In 2024, she was named to the [[Grist (magazine)|Grist]] 50 list.<ref>{{cite web | title=Grist 50 2024 | url=https://grist.org/fix/grist-50/2024/#jennifer-wilcox }}</ref>

==Memberships==
She was selected as a member of the second cohort of the Department of Energy's Oppenheimer Energy Sciences Leadership Group.<ref name=":1" />

Wilcox is a member of the [[American Institute of Chemical Engineers]], the [[American Chemical Society]], the [[North American Membrane Society]], and the [[Ninety-Nines]] (the international organization of women pilots).<ref name=":1" />

She is a Senior Fellow at the [[World Resources Institute]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Department of Energy Announces New Senior Leaders|url=https://www.energy.gov/articles/department-energy-announces-new-senior-leaders|access-date=2021-04-22|website=Energy.gov|language=en}}</ref>

== Publications ==
Wilcox is the first author to publish a textbook on carbon capture.<ref name=":1" /> Her book, ''Carbon Capture'' published in March 2012, discusses the fundamental chemical concepts ranging from thermodynamics, combustion, kinetics, mass transfer, material properties, and the relationship between the chemistry and process of carbon capture technologies.

Wilcox started the Frontiers in Climate ''Negative Emissions Technologies'' Journal with co-editor Phil Renforth.

== Personal life ==
Wilcox is married and has one daughter. They live in [[Philadelphia]].<ref>{{Cite journal |date=2020-06-16 |title=Jennifer Wilcox to Lead Carbon Dioxide Removal as WRI Senior Fellow |url=https://www.wri.org/news/release-jennifer-wilcox-lead-carbon-dioxide-removal-wri-senior-fellow |journal=World Resources Institute |language=en}}</ref>
